analysis.title: GS Vol Views 21 Oct 2026
key_insights: After a brief vol spike on Friday, markets retraced almost all of the move by Tuesday's close. Friday brought the largest one-day steepening of SPX near-term put-call skew in over two years, which flattened by an equivalent amount over the next two sessions.
Desk flows lack meaningful directional conviction. Investors are waiting for a clearing event, with earnings, FOMC, midterms and geopolitics dominating client conversations.
The micro is in focus for the rest of the week, with prints from META, TSLA, LRCX, TXN and IBM. The implied move through Friday is 0.92%.
The GS HF VIP long-short pair (GSTHVIPP) dropped another 7% over the last 10 trading days. SPX average-stock 1m ATM implied vol is about 37v, still below the late July highs near 44v.

META reports after the close. The stock is 27% above its August lows, length is 8/10 per the GS cash desk, and near-term put-call skew is flat at the 20th percentile vs 10 years, which the desk reads as constructive positioning. The implied move of 6.57% is cheap against a 9.9% average realized move over the past 5 prints.

GS prime brokerage shows short sales outpacing long buys 5:1 month to date, and short leverage is close to 5-year highs. The highest short-interest basket sits 18% below its YTD highs and is near oversold RSI levels.
Friday's panic was concentrated in the VIX market. 1.85mm VIX calls traded, one of the highest single-session call volumes since 2018.
Asset managers entered Friday with VIX futures positioning at the shortest level on record. The desk expects slightly cleaner dealer positioning after the VIX expiry.

Since the first round of the Brazil elections, EWZ vol flows have turned defensive and near-term skew has steepened to all-time highs. The desk puts the odds of a Bolsonaro victory at about 80% and likes adding upside exposure to Brazilian equities ahead of Sunday's runoff.

GS is offering an option on implied dispersion that removes the realized component. The underlying is a package of forward-starting straddles on a pre-defined basket, struck on the option's maturity date, with 2-way markets on calls and puts.
